before.title: 7G-DCT (724.0) Dual-Clutch Transmission Shudder and Mechatronics Failure
before.description: The 7-speed dual-clutch automatic (7G-DCT, transmission code 724.0) fitted to CLA 200/220/250 models develops a noticeable shudder or jolt during low-speed engagement and when shifting from 2nd to 3rd under moderate throttle. Causes include wet multi-plate clutch wear, degraded/contaminated transmission fluid, and failure of the electronic mechatronics (valve body/TCM) unit that controls clutch pressures and gear engagement. Owners also report hard or delayed engagement when coming to a stop and shifting into P/N/R, plus jerky take-off. The DCT is highly sensitive to fluid condition (MB spec 236.21) and outdated control software.
before.solution: Start with a transmission service: full fluid + filter change using MB 236.21 spec oil (recommended every ~60,000 km / 40k miles) and a TCM software update plus clutch adaptation/relearn. Persistent shudder or slipping requires clutch pack replacement; electronic shifting faults and adaptation failures typically require mechatronics (valve body) repair or replacement.
symptoms: Hard or delayed engagement into P/N/R when stopping

before.title: Auxiliary (Backup) Battery Malfunction Warning
before.description: CLA owners frequently see an 'Auxiliary Battery Malfunction' message on the dash. The CLA uses a small secondary 12V battery to support electronics and the start/stop system; it typically degrades after roughly 4-6 years. A weak auxiliary battery, or a charging fault (alternator/voltage regulator, loose connections), triggers the warning and can cause intermittent electrical glitches in the infotainment, lighting and start/stop function, sometimes with a stored 9062 fault.
before.solution: Test and replace the auxiliary battery (a low-cost part located near/behind the engine bay fuse area); clear codes after replacement. If the warning returns, diagnose the charging system — check alternator/voltage regulator output and clean/secure ground and battery connections. Verify the main starter battery health at the same time, as it is the CLA's most common breakdown cause per ADAC data.

before.title: M270/M274 Camshaft Breakage from Defective Weld (Engine Stall) — Safety Recall
before.description: On certain 2015-2016 CLA-Class cars with the 2.0L turbo M270/M274 engine, one or both camshafts were manufactured with a weld outside specification. The defective weld can fail and cause the camshaft to break, damaging the engine, causing sudden loss of power and an engine stall while driving. This is the subject of NHTSA safety recall 15V662 (covering CLA, GLA and SLK). Separately, owners more broadly report camshaft-adjuster rattle/wear on these engines that should not be confused with the recalled welded-camshaft defect.
before.solution: Check the VIN against NHTSA recall 15V662; affected cars receive a free camshaft inspection and replacement at a Mercedes dealer. Any cold-start metallic clatter that persists more than a few seconds or rough running/misfire on an M270/M274 warrants prompt inspection of the camshafts and timing/adjuster components before catastrophic failure.
symptoms: Metallic rattle/clatter from top of engine

before.title: Panoramic Roof Front Panel Detachment — Safety Recall
before.description: On 2014-2020 CLA models the front roof panel located between the windshield and the panoramic sunroof can be improperly bonded, so the adhesive fails and the panel can deteriorate and detach from the vehicle while driving. before.solution: Check the VIN against NHTSA recalls 21V197 and 23V854; affected vehicles receive a free replacement of the front roof panel installed with the correct approved adhesive at a Mercedes dealer. Owners noticing wind noise, lifting, or movement of the front roof trim should have it inspected immediately.

before.title: Premature Rear Brake Wear and Caliper Piston Sticking
before.description: CLA owners report rear brake pads and rotors wearing out before the fronts, with early 'Check Brake Pad Wear' warnings (some as low as ~50k miles) and rear rotor warping/vibration. A commonly cited root cause is the rear caliper piston sticking/dragging — a problem owners and independent mechanics say Mercedes is aware of on CLA and C-Class — which keeps the pad in contact with the rotor, accelerating wear and causing noise. Brake squeal from glazed rotors/worn pads is also common.
before.solution: Replace rear pads and rotors together (new pads on warped/grooved rotors stay noisy), and service or replace any sticking caliper — clean and lubricate slide pins and the piston, or rebuild/replace the caliper if the piston is seized. Apply brake grease to the pad backing/contact points to reduce squeal. Confirm the parking-brake actuator (electric on later cars) is releasing fully.

before.title: Water Leaks into Trunk and Rear Footwell (Vent Flap / Seam Sealing)
before.description: CLA owners report water collecting in the trunk and pooling in the rear footwells, sometimes enough to soak carpets and risk corrosion and electrical faults. A common path is poorly sealing rear pressure-relief vent flaps and water tracking down inside the trunk lid around the tail-light cluster, then into the body. Owners also cite weak factory seam sealer on spot-welded roof/rear upper body panels and door seals that let rainwater seep onto sills.
before.solution: Trace the leak: re-seal or replace the rear vent (pressure-equalization) flaps, reseal the tail-light gaskets and trunk-lid drain/seam areas with appropriate sealant, and inspect/replace door and trunk weatherstrips. Dry out saturated carpet/insulation to prevent mildew and corrosion, and check for related water damage to rear electrical modules.
symptoms: Water streaks on door sills/running boards

citations.title: Water leak in right hand side rear footwell — Mercedes CLA Forum

before.solution: Update the infotainment firmware to the latest version. Perform a hard reset by disconnecting the battery for 15 minutes. If the head unit has failed internally, replacement costs $800-1,500.

before.title: Front Suspension Strut Noise
before.description: The front struts and strut mount bearings develop clunking and creaking noises over bumps. The CLA shares its platform with the A-Class and both suffer from the same strut mount bearing wear issue, especially on models with sport suspension.
before.solution: Replace the front strut mount bearings first as the cheapest fix. If noise remains, replace the full strut assemblies with OEM or Sachs replacements. Alignment required after strut replacement.
symptoms: Clunking from front end over bumps
Creaking when turning the steering wheel while parked

before.title: Turbo Oil Leak (M270)
before.description: The M270 2.0L turbo engine develops oil leaks from the turbo oil feed and return lines. Oil drips onto the hot exhaust manifold, producing smoke and a burning oil smell. The turbo oil return line gasket is the most common leak point.
before.solution: Replace the turbo oil return line gasket and o-rings. Clean all oil residue from the exhaust to stop the burning smell. Use new crush washers on the banjo bolt fittings.

citations.title: MBWorld.org - CLA250 M270 turbo oil leak diagnosis and gasket replacement

communityRecommendations.content: Check the oil level every 1,000 miles if you notice a burning smell. The leak is slow but steady, and running low on oil with a turbo engine is catastrophic.
